text:
support_jess: FYI escalating — CS reported a customer seeing intermittent p99 spikes on /v1/generate during high-concurrency bursts. Sending sample req IDs and a curl repro.

support_jess: Basic details: region us-west-2, model: redwood-1-medium, observed at ~20:02-20:10 UTC. Concurrency reported ~16-24 from the customer. Tokens per request ~900 prompt + up to 600 gen (worst-case).

support_jess: Request IDs: req_20260317_aa1, req_20260317_ab2, req_20260317_ac3. Customer attached one error snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T20:03:12.482Z ERROR inference-runtime: request=req_20260317_aa1 latency=11.2s status=200 note="kv-cache-evict/queue-backlog"
2026-03-17T20:03:12.483Z WARN  gpu-scheduler: backlog=12 queue-ms=4800
```

monitoring_bot: Alert: gen-service p99 latency 11.2s (us-west-2) at 2026-03-17T20:03:12Z — spike correlated with sustained concurrency >16.

eng_oncall_tom: Thanks Jess. Can you confirm whether customer saw any 5xxs or auth errors? Also need a minimal curl repro we can run locally and the exact concurrency pattern (burst size, qps).

support_jess: No 5xxs, only long tail p99s (200 responses). Customer says burst pattern = ramp to 20 concurrent requests over ~30s, sustaining ~20 for 90s, then drops. They can reproduce consistently.

devex_omar: If customer can share curl + one request ID, ask them to add header `X-Request-ID: <req>` so we can tie it. Provide a curl like this to reproduce: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_20260317_rep1" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-medium","input":"<long prompt here>","max_tokens":600}'
```

support_mike: Also request they run our debug bundle helper so we get full logs: `/debug-bundle --request req_20260317_aa1 --include-system-logs` (internal helper). If they can't run it, ask them to upload the client-side timing CSV and their cURL command.

eng_oncall_tom: OK. From the runtime snippet it looks like KV cache eviction / queue backlog. Need server-side traces for those request IDs and the scheduler snapshot. @ml_infra_anya can you pull traces for those req IDs and run a quick repro with concurrency 24 and token profile (prompt 900 + gen 600)? If you want a smaller set, try 16 first.

ml_infra_anya: Will do. I'll run an internal load test with the same token profile and ramp pattern. Saving a repro pack: prompt_set/2026-03-17/ with 5 prompts (varying lengths), concurrency targets [16,24,32], token targets [1200,1500].

ml_infra_anya: Quick question — should we include streaming vs non-streaming mode? Customer uses non-streaming.

eng_oncall_tom: Non-streaming to match customer. Also include a run with `--prefix-cache` enabled & disabled to see cache hit differences.

support_jess: Customer also mentioned slightly different behavior when using embeddings pipeline before generation (small warmup requests). I'll note that in the pack.

devex_omar: For the curl repro, recommend using `ab`/`hey`/`wrk` or a small Python script that fires concurrent POSTs with identical prompts to mimic cache pressure. Example Python snippet to run 20 concurrent tasks: 
```
# (pseudo)
import requests,concurrent.futures
url='https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
headers={'Authorization':'Bearer REDWOOD_API_KEY','Content-Type':'application/json','X-Request-ID':'test-1'}
payload={"model":"redwood-1-medium","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":600}
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(20) as e:
  futures=[e.submit(requests.post,url,headers=headers,json=payload) for _ in range(20)]
  for f in futures: print(f.result().status_code)
```

support_mike: I'm collecting the customer's curl and timings now and will upload to the shared bucket. Uploading to: s3://redwood-support/repro-packs/2026-03-17/client-acme-latency/ (will post link once done).

support_jess: Attached their small prompt set (3 prompts) and a CSV of client latencies. Preliminary median ~350ms, p95 ~1.4s, p99 ~11s during bursts.

ml_infra_anya: Thanks. I'll run three load tests: concurrency=16,24,32; durations 2 minutes each, non-streaming, token caps 1200 and 1500. Will capture GPU utilization, scheduler queue depth, and KV cache stats.

eng_oncall_tom: If the repro reproduces, next step is to try with quantized model variant and smaller batch window to see if scheduling/batching is the culprit. Also capture `inference.log` and `gpu-scheduler` snapshots.

support_jess: Customer is on a reserved Dedicated instance (dedicated-pool-id: dp-7b9), they requested us to escalate. They can provide continuous reproduction windows tomorrow morning PST.

monitoring_bot: Note: Related alert group opened INC-2026-7312 (latency regression group).

devex_omar: One more ask — include the exact prompt tokenization counts per prompt (we need tokenizers to reproduce). Attach output of `tokenize --model redwood-1-medium prompt.txt` if possible.

support_mike: Uploaded: s3://redwood-support/repro-packs/2026-03-17/client-acme-latency/payloads.tar.gz (includes curl, prompts, client-timings.csv). Link expires in 7 days.

ml_infra_anya: Starting run now. Will paste summarized traces and upload the internal debug bundle to the same s3 path once collected. ETA ~30–45m.

eng_oncall_tom: Great. If we see kv-cache-evict events correlated with latency, we'll try two mitigations: 1) increase cache capacity for dp-7b9 in us-west-2 for a short window, 2) reduce batching window to lower queue latency.

support_jess: Noted. I'll keep CS looped in and get customer permission for temporary config changes if needed.

ml_infra_anya: Run complete — early result: p99 reproduced at concurrency=24 with token=1500. Uploading bundle now: s3://redwood-support/repro-packs/2026-03-17/client-acme-latency/internal-bundle-174.tar.gz. Summary: scheduler queue depth spiked to 18, backpressure caused delayed worker assignment, KV cache churn observed.

eng_oncall_tom: Thanks Anya. I'll open a follow-up with mitigation plan and a canary change: lower batching window from 20ms to 10ms for dp-7b9 during the customer's window and monitor.

support_jess: Customer okayed the canary. I'll schedule the change for 2026-03-18 16:00 PST.

support_mike: Closing loop with CS and document findings in INC-2026-7312. :white_check_mark:

ml_infra_anya: Leaving logs and trace IDs in the bundle metadata: traces: [req_20260317_aa1, req_20260317_ab2, req_20260317_ac3]. If you need raw scheduler metrics, tell me which time slice.

eng_oncall_tom: Good job team. We'll follow up after the canary. :thumbsup:
